title: CATARACT 2, MULTIPLE TYPES
alt_titles: CATARACT 2, MULTIPLE TYPES, WITH OR WITHOUT MICROCORNEA

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that cataract-2 (CTRCT2), which comprises several types of cataract, is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gamma-C-crystallin gene (CRYGC; 123680) on chromosome 2q33.3.

checks.claim: Cataract-2 (CTRCT2) comprises several types of cataract.
checks.evidence_quote: This is the first case of phenotypic heterogeneity in the primary congenital cataract specifically associated with the R168W mutation in the CRYGC gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract shows that CRYGC mutation is linked to more than one cataract type: nuclear in this family and lamellar in an earlier report. It does not use the CTRCT2 designation.

checks.claim: Cataract-2 (CTRCT2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gamma-C-crystallin gene (CRYGC).
checks.evidence_quote: DNA sequencing analysis of the CRYGA-D gene cluster of the affected members showed the heterozygous missense mutation c.502C>T in the CRYGC gene.
checks.explanation: In this autosomal dominant family, the heterozygous CRYGC mutation segregates with congenital cataract.

checks.claim: The CRYGC gene is located on chromosome 2q33.3.
checks.evidence_quote: We have localized the cataracts to a 19-cM interval on chromosome 2q33-q35 including the gamma-crystallin gene cluster.
checks.explanation: The paper gives only a linkage interval of 2q33-q35 containing the gamma-crystallin cluster. The specific band 2q33.3 for CRYGC is not stated.

paragraphs.text: Mutations in the CRYGC gene have been found in several forms of congenital cataract (Zhang et al., 2009). These include Coppock-like (nuclear) cataract (Héon et al., 1999), zonular pulverulent cataract (Ren et al., 2000), and lamellar cataract (Gonzalez-Huerta et al., 2007). Some affected individuals also have microcornea (Zhang et al., 2009). Inheritance is autosomal dominant (Ren et al., 2000).

checks.claim: Mutations in the CRYGC gene have been found in several forms of congenital cataract.
checks.evidence_quote: there are four other mutations in CRYGC that have been associated with cataracts including Coppock-like cataracts (T5P), variable zonular pulverulent cataracts (5 bp duplication), lamellar cataracts (R168W), nuclear cataracts (R168W), and nuclear cataracts (C109X).
checks.explanation: The paper lists CRYGC mutations linked to several types of cataract.

checks.claim: CRYGC mutations cause Coppock-like (nuclear) cataract.
checks.evidence_quote: Further analysis of the original Coppock-like-cataract family identified a missense mutation in a highly conserved segment of exon 2 of CRYGC.
checks.explanation: The abstract links a CRYGC missense mutation to Coppock-like cataract. It does not call the cataract 'nuclear', so that detail is unsupported here.

checks.claim: CRYGC mutations cause zonular pulverulent cataract.
checks.evidence_quote: A 5-base insertion in the gammaC-crystallin gene is associated with autosomal dominant variable zonular pulverulent cataract.
checks.explanation: The title links a CRYGC mutation to zonular pulverulent cataract.

checks.claim: CRYGC mutations cause lamellar cataract.
checks.evidence_quote: This mutation has been associated with the phenotype of lamellar cataract but is also considered a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) in the NCBI database.
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions lamellar cataract only as the type an earlier report linked to R168W. The family in this paper had nuclear congenital cataract, so citing Gonzalez-Huerta et al. (2007) for lamellar cataract is misleading.

checks.claim: Some individuals with CRYGC-related cataract also have microcornea.
checks.evidence_quote: the present study has identified a novel nonsense W157X mutation in CRYGC associated with autosomal dominant cataracts and microcornea in a four-generation Chinese family.
checks.explanation: The paper reports a CRYGC mutation in a family where affected members have both cataract and microcornea.

checks.claim: CRYGC-related cataract is inherited in an autosomal dominant manner.
checks.evidence_quote: A seven-generation family with 30 members affected by highly variable autosomal dominant zonular pulverulent cataracts has been previously described.
checks.explanation: The paper describes autosomal dominant inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Ren et al. (2000) and Li et al. (2012) each reported a family in which CRYGC-related cataract was inherited as an autosomal dominant trait.

checks.claim: Ren et al. (2000) reported a family in which CRYGC-related cataract was inherited as an autosomal dominant trait.
checks.evidence_quote: A seven-generation family with 30 members affected by highly variable autosomal dominant zonular pulverulent cataracts has been previously described.
checks.explanation: This is a single family with autosomal dominant cataract caused by a CRYGC mutation.

checks.claim: Li et al. (2012) reported a family in which CRYGC-related cataract was inherited as an autosomal dominant trait.
checks.evidence_quote: in a three-generation Chinese family with autosomal dominant congenital nuclear cataract by sequencing candidate genes
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a family with autosomal dominant congenital nuclear cataract carrying a heterozygous CRYGC mutation.

paragraphs.text: Lubsen et al. (1987) found that the locus for Coppock-like cataract was closely linked to the gamma-crystallin gene cluster.

checks.claim: The locus for Coppock-like cataract is closely linked to the gamma-crystallin gene cluster.
checks.evidence_quote: The absolute correlation between the presence of haplotype P and cataract within this family shows that the gamma-crystallin gene cluster and the locus for the Coppock-like cataract are closely linked
checks.explanation: The abstract states this linkage directly and gives a maximum lod score of 7.58 at theta = 0.

paragraphs.text: Congenital cataract is genetically heterogeneous (Zhang et al., 2009). Héon et al. (1999) found that mutation in the CRYGD gene, which lies in the same gamma-crystallin gene cluster on chromosome 2q33-q35 as CRYGC, causes a separate form of cataract.

checks.claim: Congenital cataract is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: Congenital cataract is a clinically and genetically heterogeneous lens disorder
checks.explanation: The paper says this directly.

checks.claim: The CRYGD gene lies in the same gamma-crystallin gene cluster on chromosome 2q33-q35 as CRYGC.
checks.evidence_quote: We recently mapped the aculeiform cataract to the gamma-crystallin locus (CRYG) on chromosome 2q33-35, and mutational analysis of the CRYG-genes cluster identified the aculeiform-cataract mutation in exon 2 of gamma-crystallin D (CRYGD).
checks.explanation: The abstract places CRYGD in the CRYG gene cluster on 2q33-35. CRYGC is another gamma-crystallin gene examined in the same study.

checks.claim: Mutation in the CRYGD gene causes a form of cataract separate from CRYGC-related cataract.
checks.evidence_quote: mutational analysis of the CRYG-genes cluster identified the aculeiform-cataract mutation in exon 2 of gamma-crystallin D (CRYGD).
checks.explanation: The CRYGD mutation causes aculeiform cataract, which is a different form from the Coppock-like cataract linked to CRYGC.

paragraphs.text: Héon et al. (1999) studied cataract families linked to the gamma-crystallin gene cluster. In the original family with Coppock-like cataract, they identified a missense mutation in a highly conserved segment of exon 2 of the CRYGC gene.

checks.claim: Héon et al. (1999) studied cataract families linked to the gamma-crystallin gene cluster.
checks.evidence_quote: We recently mapped the aculeiform cataract to the gamma-crystallin locus (CRYG) on chromosome 2q33-35, and mutational analysis of the CRYG-genes cluster
checks.explanation: The study analyzed cataract families mapped to the CRYG locus: the aculeiform family and the original Coppock-like family.

checks.claim: In the original family with Coppock-like cataract, Héon et al. (1999) identified a missense mutation in the CRYGC gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Further analysis of the original Coppock-like-cataract family identified a missense mutation in a highly conserved segment of exon 2 of CRYGC.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The CRYGC missense mutation in the original Coppock-like cataract family lies in a highly conserved segment of exon 2.
checks.evidence_quote: Further analysis of the original Coppock-like-cataract family identified a missense mutation in a highly conserved segment of exon 2 of CRYGC.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Ren et al. (2000) studied a family with autosomal dominant variable zonular pulverulent cataract. They identified a heterozygous 5-bp duplication (insertion) in the CRYGC gene that disrupted the reading frame and was predicted to result in a truncated protein.

checks.claim: Ren et al. (2000) studied a family with autosomal dominant variable zonular pulverulent cataract.
checks.evidence_quote: A 5-base insertion in the gammaC-crystallin gene is associated with autosomal dominant variable zonular pulverulent cataract.
checks.explanation: The title states this directly.

checks.claim: In a family with variable zonular pulverulent cataract, Ren et al. (2000) identified a 5-bp duplication (insertion) in the CRYGC gene.
checks.evidence_quote: a 5-bp duplication within exon 2 of the gammaC-crystallin gene has been found in one allele of each affected family member
checks.explanation: The title calls it a 5-base insertion and the abstract calls it a 5-bp duplication, which matches the claim.

checks.claim: The 5-bp CRYGC duplication in the zonular pulverulent cataract family was heterozygous.
checks.evidence_quote: has been found in one allele of each affected family member
checks.explanation: Found in one allele means the duplication is heterozygous.

checks.claim: The 5-bp CRYGC duplication disrupted the reading frame.
checks.evidence_quote: This mutation disrupts the reading frame of the gammaC-crystallin coding sequence
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The 5-bp CRYGC duplication was predicted to result in a truncated protein.
checks.evidence_quote: is predicted to result in the synthesis of an unstable gammaC-crystallin with 38 amino acids of the first "Greek key" motif followed by 52 random amino acids
checks.explanation: A protein of 38 normal residues followed by 52 frameshifted residues is a predicted truncated protein. The paper also calls it unstable.

paragraphs.text: Santhiya et al. (2002) reported novel mutations in the gamma-crystallin genes causing autosomal dominant congenital cataract.

checks.claim: Santhiya et al. (2002) reported novel mutations in the gamma-crystallin genes.
checks.evidence_quote: Novel mutations in the gamma-crystallin genes cause autosomal dominant congenital cataracts.
checks.explanation: The title says novel mutations were found in the gamma-crystallin genes.

checks.claim: The novel gamma-crystallin gene mutations reported by Santhiya et al. (2002) cause autosomal dominant congenital cataract.
checks.evidence_quote: Novel mutations in the gamma-crystallin genes cause autosomal dominant congenital cataracts.
checks.explanation: The title says these mutations cause autosomal dominant congenital cataracts.

paragraphs.text: In a family with autosomal dominant variable zonular pulverulent cataract, Ren et al. (2000) found a heterozygous 5-bp duplication in the CRYGC gene. The duplication disrupted the reading frame and was predicted to result in a truncated protein.

checks.claim: In a family with autosomal dominant variable zonular pulverulent cataract, Ren et al. (2000) found a 5-bp duplication in the CRYGC gene.
checks.evidence_quote: a 5-bp duplication within exon 2 of the gammaC-crystallin gene has been found in one allele of each affected family member
checks.explanation: The duplication was found in the family with autosomal dominant variable zonular pulverulent cataract.

checks.claim: The 5-bp CRYGC duplication in the zonular pulverulent cataract family was heterozygous.
checks.evidence_quote: has been found in one allele of each affected family member
checks.explanation: Found in one allele means the duplication is heterozygous.

checks.claim: The 5-bp CRYGC duplication disrupted the reading frame.
checks.evidence_quote: This mutation disrupts the reading frame of the gammaC-crystallin coding sequence
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The 5-bp CRYGC duplication was predicted to result in a truncated protein.
checks.evidence_quote: is predicted to result in the synthesis of an unstable gammaC-crystallin with 38 amino acids of the first "Greek key" motif followed by 52 random amino acids
checks.explanation: The predicted product is a truncated frameshift protein.
